newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian separatists urge boycott of anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Indian separatists urge boycott of anniversary.

text.p: Four separatist groups in India's remote northeastern state of Manipur on Tuesday urged people to boycott the nation's independence day celebrations.
India marks its 50th anniversary of independence from British colonial rule on August 15.

The People's Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak, United National Liberation Front, Kangleipak Communist Party and Kangle Yawol Kana Lup appealed in a statement for people to stay at home and observe a "public curfew" from 7 p.m (1330 GMT) on August 14 to 6 p.m. (1230 GMT) on August 15.

Dozens of separatist groups have for decades waged armed struggles for independent homelands in India's northeast, which comprises seven states with more than 200 ethnic groups and is rich in minerals and timber.
The hilly, heavily-forested region is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and linked to the rest of India only by a 20-km (12-mile) wide corridor.
